panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Gross pathology from a colorectal juvenile polyp in the son, shown adjacent to normal mucosa. The caption explicitly identifies this as one of two polyps establishing juvenile polyposis syndrome. B: Magnified H&E section of the region selected from panel A demonstrates the captioned characteristic histology of a typical juvenile colorectal polyp. C: Gross pathology from the second colorectal polyp in the son, shown adjacent to normal mucosa. The caption explicitly identifies both lesions as juvenile polyps. D: Magnified H&E section of the region selected from panel C demonstrates characteristic juvenile-polyp histology, directly attributed to a patient whose diagnosis of juvenile polyposis syndrome was confirmed.
panels.attribution_text: Gao et al. Juvenile polyposis syndrome might be misdiagnosed as familial adenomatous polyposis: a case report and literature review.. BMC gastroenterology 2020. doi:10.1186/s12876-020-01238-7. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 5.
panels.figure_caption: Pathological manifestation of two examined colorectal polyps in the son. a Gross appearance of one polyp. The left half was the polyp, and the right half was normal mucosa. b Magnified image of the selected rectangular area from panel a, showing typical juvenile polyp, with cystically dilated glands, abundant mucus in the gland cavity, cuboidal epithelium, abundance of edematous lamina propria. c Gross appearance of the other polyp. The right half was the polyp, and the left half was normal mucosa. d: Magnified image of the selected rectangular area from panel c, showing typical juvenile polyp
in_text_mentions: uboidal or columnar epithelium, abundance of edematous lamina propria with inflammatory cells, and the absence of smooth muscle in the stroma. No dysplasia or cancer was evident in these polyps (Fig. 5). All examined polyps were proved to be typical juvenile polyps, so the diagnosis of JPS was confirmed in the son. He remains in excellent condition with normal sexual and urinary functions. His fecal frequency was once per day at one year after surgery.
